newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Western Australia oil output seen set to rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Western Australia oil output seen set to rise.

text.p: Despite a drop in oil production in 1995/96 (July-June), output in Western Australia is poised for growth, the Western Australia government said on Wednesday.

The state's crude oil production declined 3.2 percent in 1995/96 (July-June) to 59.99 million barrels, or 163,908 barrels per day from the previous year's output of 61.96 million barrels, or 169,756 bpd, figures from the Western Australian Oil & Gas Review journal show.

The government-published journal links the the fall in oil production to a natural decline in output from current oil fields and a number of shut downs caused by cyclonic weather and maintenance work.
Production from the Wanaea and Cossack offshore fields of the North West Shelf should almost triple in the current year to an average of about 90,000 bpd, the journal said.
Also, full development of the Wandoo oil field is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 1997, which will lift output to up to 40,000 bpd from the current 12,696 bpd,it said.

Total crude oil and condensate production in Western Australia averaged 244,000 bpd in 1995/96 against 211,000 bpd in Victoria state, making it Australia's biggest oil and gas producing state, the figures show.
This reflects the start of a number of new fields developments in the last three years, including the Griffin, Scindian, Chinook, Roller Skate, Goodwyn, Cossack and Wanaea projects, the journal said.
